ACTION 04 OF 32 · PHASE 01

Build the pass-or-fail checklist

Define what 'good enough to proceed' looks like at each business gate.

WHEN TO DO THISBefore spending on design, subscriptions or registration.ESTIMATED WORK TIME15 min
↗
Your one job

Define what 'good enough to proceed' looks like at each business gate.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    Write minimum quality standards for demand evidence, margins, delivery capacity, security and customer experience.

  2. 02

    Write red flags that pause the project: no clear buyer, negative unit economics, missing permit, poor supplier reliability.

  3. 03

    Set specific acceptance tests for the website: mobile readability, working inquiry flow, real contact info, basic performance and real assets.

  4. 04

    Ask ChatGPT to critique the business against these rules at the end of each phase.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Create a founder QA scorecard for this business with six dimensions: Demand, Economics, Delivery, Legality, Trust, and Technical Reliability. For each dimension give: the required evidence, minimum pass rule, serious red flags and the smallest next test. Use blanks instead of invented thresholds. End with a decision: PROCEED / TEST MORE / STOP, justified by my real evidence.
03

Finish with this

A go/no-go checklist to reuse throughout the build.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • Six business dimensions have evidence requirements
  • Red flags are explicitly written
  • A clear next test exists for each unknown
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

A 9/10 subjective rating is not evidence that customers will pay.

READY TO MOVE ON?

A person unfamiliar with the idea can read the brief and understand the problem, buyer, offer, constraints and what's still unknown.
